title: Advice on starting in personal management; why he has no license
summary: Thomas advises getting the right agent, explains why he never took an agency license, and Bill Doggett and Bill Davis leaving him.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Well, what do you suggest for a young man that had been a musician and would like to follow in your footsteps and use his expertise as a musician and wanted to go into personal management? Since you made some mistakes, you said, what would you suggest he do?
Well, the most important thing is getting involved with the right booking agent. The agent has got to...
Well, what about them starting one of their own, Foots?
Well, they can do that if they get an artist that's popular.
So what you'd do, you would analyze what's popular then, and look for an artist that's popular. Can you start that way first?
Well, yeah...
Is it an unwritten rule that you can't get a booking agency? Is that a hard thing to get?
Thomas - 200
Well, I found out in my situation, I used to think that I was a musician and I could book. Any musician can book himself anywhere.
But can you get a booking... You can get a license.
Yeah, I can get a license.
Do you have a license?
No, I don't have a license.
Well, why? Why wouldn't you have one?
Well, at the time I tried to book, the artists would up... They'd put their money where you couldn't book them. You either had a price where you would get booked, or you've overpriced yourself.
Well, the (?) can do if you have your license.. If you couldn't book them, there's still the license(?)... You could book me, and I'd say, "Well, I want a hundred dollars if you've got the license."
Yeah. I don't think I'd have any trouble getting a license. Because you know, the...
Well, you've been in business forty years. Why don't you have one?
Well, at the time I tried to get into it, the expenses were bigger than I was making any money. And I didn't have any artist that was bookable, so I just finally
Thomas - 201
got out of it.
A musician can get into Local 802 here ..(?).. for $100.
Yeah, I could have got in. I'd have to apply to...
And then you can get some (?) for $200.
Right. That's what you've got to get first. You've got to get the place...
Yeah. Then you have to have a place of establishment.
Right. You have to have a place and a business.
You've got to be able to go into a (?) building like (?) is working out of.
Right. Because they have to check all that...
That's what (?) used to do.

Right. To make it.. It's a possibility, if I could have kept... There's two guys that I had a lot to do with...about half(?) of the time I had to do with them being a star. And they both went to (?)Net City(?) on me.
Went where?
(?)Net City(?). You see, if I'd have had the...
Thomas - 202
Who were they?
Bill Davis and Bill Doggett.
Well, they're still around, aren't they.

Yeah. But Bill got so you would give him a deal on a place he could go, and he'd undermine you and he'd want to book it himself. And when he left me, I just forgot him. I was in the booking business and I was making money, so I didn't have to worry about Bill Doggett. He was the first one to leave. And Bill Davis, I forget why he left. But see...
